## Summarize data

In this milestone, you'll use group-wise summaries to compute the Cumulative Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) for each index.

## Recreation

### Part 1 - Import

```{r}
#| label: recreation-import

```

### Part 2 - Compute CAGR

We can compute the CAGR for one index like so. Run the code below to compute the CAGR for the S&P 500 index.

```{r}
#| label: compute-cagr
#| eval: false
indexes |>
  filter(symbol == "^GSPC") |>
  summarise(CAGR = ((last(adjusted) / first(adjusted)) - 1) * 100)
```

Now, you'll compute the CAGR as above for each index. Run the code below to see a table.

```{r}
#| label: recreate-this
#| message: false
solution <- readr::read_csv("data/milestone02.csv")
solution
```

Your task is to use what you've learned about the dplyr package to transform `indexes` into this table. You will need to:

1. Group the data
2. Summarize to compute the Cumulative Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) for each index

Run the following code chunk to test whether you have the same answer as the solution:

```{r}

#| eval: false
waldo::compare(index_cagrs, solution, tolerance = 1e-4)
```
